reasoning: Proof: For a prime p and positive integer n, let v_p(n) be the exponent of p in the prime factorization of n. Then v_p(a^2) = 2·v_p(a) and v_p(b^2) = 2·v_p(b). If a^2 | b^2, then for every prime p, v_p(a^2) ≤ v_p(b^2), i.e., 2·v_p(a) ≤ 2·v_p(b), so v_p(a) ≤ v_p(b). Since this holds for every prime p, a | b. (Equivalently: let g = gcd(a,b), a = g·a', b = g·b' with gcd(a',b') = 1. Then a'^2 | b'^2 with gcd(a'^2, b'^2) = 1 forces a'^2 = 1, so a' = 1 and a = g | b.)
